New Program Proposal Walkthrough
New Program Proposal Walkthrough
This guide provides step-by-step procedural instructions for completing and submitting a New Program Proposal in Kuali. It focuses on navigating the form, including what to select or enter in each field.
*In Kuali, Programs refer to Degrees, Majors, Minors & Certificates.
The guide is organized by proposal section (panel), so you can jump directly to a section when you need help.
This guide does not provide guidance on course content or academic decisions. Consult your department and applicable curriculum committees for questions about developing the course itself.

The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.
Additional Proposer(s) Use this section to identify additional individuals who can speak to the proposed program. Individuals listed here will not receive Kuali notifications or have access to edit the proposal. Their inclusion simply provides transparency to the reviewing committees about who else is involved in or can speak to the proposal.

Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the program to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term Select the term and year in which you anticipate the first students will graduate with this credential.
Credential Type Select the type of credential you are proposing: Degree, Major, Minor, or Certificate.
Level Select the level of the program: Undergraduate, Graduate, or Dual Currently, the only Dual Degree program offered at URI is the Pharm.D.
Academic Calendar Select the academic calendar for the program: Accelerated 7-week through URI Online, or Traditional 14-week with Summer and J-Term Sessions.
Program Locations Select all locations where the program will be offered.
College Select the college in which the program is housed.
Department Select the department in which the program is housed.
CIP Code Enter the specific CIP code that applies to your program. You can search for your program’s code here.

Once you have finalized your proposal draft:
Select Leave Edit Mode in the upper-right corner of the screen, just below the orange bar.
Select Submit for Approval to submit the proposal to the workflow.

Your proposal will automatically be sent to the appropriate review committees. You may be contacted within Kuali Comments by the committees with questions to the proposal (an email will notify you automatically). You can also return to your proposal from your dashboard at any time to view the workflow status.

Content Overlap
Tags: courses,programs,specializations
Short Description: Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial content overlap.
Content Overlap
Proposed courses, programs, and specializations are reviewed for potential content overlap with existing curricula. Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial actual or perceived content overlap.
Early consultation with potentially affected academic units may help identify concerns, clarify distinctions between offerings, and support an efficient review process.
A letter of support, which may be provided as an email from an affected department chair, can be uploaded to the Kuali proposal to document (a) that both departments have considered potential content overlap; (b) communication between the affected department and the department proposing the curriculum; and (c) the affected department’s support for the proposed curriculum.

Specialization Description
Tags: specializations
Short Description: The University Catalog description of a program specialization, including its specialization-specific curriculum and any additional requirements for completion.
Specialization Description
The University Catalog description of the requirements for completing a specialization within an academic program, including the specialization-specific courses and credits required in addition to the program’s core requirements, as well as any additional specialization-specific requirements.

Descriptive overview: A brief paragraph explaining the purpose and significance of the specialization.
Course Requirements
Important: Do not include program requirements in the specialization description.
Only include the requirements of the specialization in the specialization description, and exclude the core requirements to the program. The specialization
A specialization is an addition to the academic program, not a second listing of the program’s requirements. Students complete the requirements of the program and, where applicable, the additional requirements of their chosen specialization. The specialization description should therefore include only the requirements that are specific to that specialization.
Repeating the program requirements within the specialization could imply that students must complete those requirements again as part of the specialization. Keeping program-wide requirements in the program description and specialization-specific requirements in the specialization description makes it clear which requirements apply to the program as a whole and which are additional requirements for the specialization.
(For ABMs only) Courses that are able to be double-counted

A minimum GPA average of 2.00 must be earned in the specialization courses (UM 8.20.61)
Half of the credits required for the specialization must be earned at URI (UM 8.20.61)
A maximum of one third of the total credits required for a master’s program may be double counted for an ABM program. (UM 8.30.19)

All new courses must be certified as having been reviewed by the faculty of the originating academic organization. Certification must be provided by the appropriate authority, which may include the Department Chair, Area Coordinator, or, in some cases, the College Curriculum Committee Chair.
The proposer should leave this section blank. The Department Chair or other authorized curriculum reviewer will complete the certification by checking the box to confirm that the course has been reviewed by the appropriate faculty, entering their name, and providing the date of certification.
Once the proposal reaches the course certification step in the workflow, it cannot move forward until the designated certifier completes this section.
